answer: One defence is stake-bonded identity: every agent locks a deposit in a shared vault before it can transact, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove fraud. A new identity starts on a narrow ledge, with low trust limits and tiny transaction caps, and only earns wider limits after honest, attested work. The velvet glove is that honest agents pay almost nothing: the stake is returned with interest once they build a record. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand deposits and slow trust climbs, so attack cost scales linearly while honest newcomers pay only time.
